property_summary: For any description, a call to newEmergencyOracle deploys an EmergencyOracle whose owner() equals the calling account (the deployer/admin here); the mutant assigns ownership to address(c) instead, so for some description the created oracle's owner is not the caller.

For any caller and description, the EmergencyOracle deployed by c.newEmergencyOracle is owned by the calling account and is never owned by address(c); the mutant assigns ownership to address(c), breaking this rule for every admissible input that successfully deploys an oracle.

For any admissible admin and description, the EmergencyOracle deployed by c.newEmergencyOracle is owned by the calling admin account; the mutant instead assigns ownership to address(c), so the oracle's owner() differs from the caller.

Any EmergencyOracle that c successfully creates via newEmergencyOracle(description) must be operationally controlled by the calling account (the caller can invoke turnOnOracle on it); the mutant assigns ownership to address(c), so the caller can no longer operate the oracle it just created.
